reason: The numbers reproduce exactly (word box top 37.0 tasks / 38.13 notes / 58.0 timeline, stable over five rail round-trips at 1920/1440/1280), but the finding's load-bearing claim — 'the vertical is aligned to nothing... nothing but padding puts it there' — is false: .tlHead's top padding is var(--stage-pad)=40px, the same single token that produces the horizontal inset the finding itself concedes is defensible, and it lands the wordmark at the page's own 40/40 inset corner (word left 140 = .b-ownerField stage left 140, sheet origin 100,18). All three verticals are governed by each product's own head token exactly as all three horizontals are (tasks centred in a 60px bar, notes in a 62px min-height bar, timeline at the page inset), so the finding calls one axis principled and the identical logic on the other axis arbitrary. The 'one motion the architecture promises will not happen' also misreads the locked promise, which is that no product is ever torn down, not that chrome shares a baseline; and the fix's literal `padding: 19px 40px 0` collides with the `--stage-pad: 0px` phone rule at src/timeline.css:384 and the ≤430px .tlHead override at src/across.css:423.
